problems.problem: Invented quote; Edmondson (1999) defined psychological safety as "a shared belief that the team is safe for interpersonal risk-taking", not "team climate for speaking up".
problems.correction: Edmondson, 1999 — "a shared belief that the team is safe for interpersonal risk-taking"
problems.verifierReason: Edmondson 1999 defines psychological safety as 'shared belief... safe for interpersonal risk-taking'; 'team climate for speaking up' is not her wording.

problems.quote: The 2nd ARC cites "islands of excellence" as minority influence nodes (Para 4.6).
problems.problem: Wrong report reference; "islands of excellence" appears in 2nd ARC's 10th Report (Personnel Administration), not the 4th Report (Ethics in Governance) Para 4.6.
problems.correction: The 2nd ARC (10th Report) cites "islands of excellence" as minority influence nodes.
problems.verifierReason: 'Islands of excellence' appears in 2nd ARC 10th Report (Personnel Administration), not 4th Report (Ethics in Governance) Para 4.6.

problems.quote: The 2nd ARC (Para 4.11) endorses "behavioural insights for public good" but warns against "paternalistic manipulation."
problems.problem: The 2nd ARC 4th Report (2007) does not use the term "behavioural insights" or "paternalistic manipulation"; these concepts post-date the report.
problems.correction: Later behavioural economics literature (e.g., Thaler & Sunstein, 2008) endorses behavioural insights for public good but warns against paternalistic manipulation.
problems.verifierReason: 2nd ARC 4th Report (2007) predates 'behavioural insights' and 'paternalistic manipulation' terminology from Thaler & Sunstein (2008).

problems.quote: The 2nd ARC (Para 4.8–4.10) identifies EI utilities across administrative work.
problems.problem: The 2nd ARC 4th Report does not discuss Emotional Intelligence; EI utilities are a later framework.
problems.correction: Contemporary frameworks identify EI utilities across administrative work.
problems.verifierReason: 2nd ARC 4th Report does not discuss Emotional Intelligence utilities; EI frameworks in administration are contemporary.

problems.quote: all central government employees below the rank of Secretary
problems.problem: The CCS (Conduct) Rules apply to all central civil servants (except All India Services), not only those below the rank of Secretary.
problems.correction: all central government employees (except All India Services)
problems.verifierReason: CCS Conduct Rules apply to all central civil servants except All India Services, not limited by rank.

problems.quote: The Central Civil Services (Conduct) Rules categorize conflicts into actual, potential and perceived conflicts.
problems.problem: The CCS (Conduct) Rules themselves do not contain this three‑fold categorization; it was introduced in later DoPT guidelines/Model Code.
problems.correction: DoPT guidelines categorize conflicts into actual, potential and perceived conflicts.
problems.verifierReason: CCS Conduct Rules lack three-fold conflict categorization; it appears in DoPT guidelines.

problems.quote: Failure to disclose or recuse attracts disciplinary action under Rule 14 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules.
problems.problem: Rule 14 deals with acceptance of gifts; conflict‑of‑interest violations are covered under Rule 18A (inserted in 2014).
problems.correction: Failure to disclose or recuse attracts disciplinary action under Rule 18A of the CCS (Conduct) Rules.
problems.verifierReason: Rule 14 covers gifts; conflict-of-interest violations fall under Rule 18A (inserted 2014).

problems.quote: the requirement that the Prime Minister’s prior approval is needed for an inquiry into the Prime Minister
problems.problem: The Lokpal Act requires approval by a Full Bench of the Lokpal, not the Prime Minister's personal approval.
problems.correction: the requirement that a Full Bench of the Lokpal approve any inquiry into the Prime Minister
problems.verifierReason: Lokpal Act requires Full Bench approval for PM inquiry, not PM's personal approval.

problems.quote: One-off training programmes have negligible impact. EI must be woven into the fabric of training, appraisal, and organisational culture.
problems.problem: The 2nd ARC did not use the term 'EI' (Emotional Intelligence) in its reports; the quote appears invented or misattributed. The 2nd ARC's recommendations concern ethics training, not emotional intelligence.
problems.correction: One-off training programmes have negligible impact. Ethics must be woven into the fabric of training, appraisal, and organisational culture.
problems.verifierReason: 2nd ARC 4th Report (Ethics in Governance) explicitly uses 'Ethics', not 'EI'. The quote is a known verbatim excerpt with 'Ethics'.

problems.problem: There was no 2015 amendment to the Whistleblower Protection Act; the 2015 amendment bill was introduced but not enacted.
problems.verifierReason: The Whistle Blowers Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2015 lapsed in Rajya Sabha; no amendment was enacted in 2015. The Act is correctly cited as 2014.

problems.quote: 2021 amendment introduced a “National Disaster Response Fund” (NDRF) with a mandatory 10 % allocation for “pre‑disaster preparedness”
problems.problem: The NDRF was established by the Disaster Management Act, 2005; the 2019 amendment created the National Disaster Mitigation Fund for pre-disaster preparedness. There was no 2021 amendment introducing the NDRF.
problems.correction: The Disaster Management Act, 2005 established the NDRF; the 2019 amendment created the National Disaster Mitigation Fund for pre-disaster preparedness.
problems.verifierReason: NDRF was created by the Disaster Management Act 2005; the 2019 amendment created the National Disaster Mitigation Fund for preparedness.
